question: The FEMYSO Association has gained increasing visibility within the EU institutions for a number of years. It has received EUR 210 0001 in EU funding – of which EUR 49 881 in 2014 and EUR 35 000 in 2015 under the Erasmus+ programme2.

A French Ministry of the Interior report on ‘The Muslim Brotherhood and Political Islamism in France’3 explicitly names FEMYSO as the ‘youth branch’ of the European Council of Muslims, which is described by the intelligence services as an organisation controlled by the Muslim Brotherhood responsible for its strategy to influence the EU institutions. 1.
What monitoring and diligence mechanisms does the Commission use when registering organisations in its calls for projects, especially to detect and exclude organisations linked to Islamism?
How does the Commission justify the EU’s support for an organisation identified by a French official report as a channel of influence for the Muslim Brotherhood?
Is the Commission willing to take into account reports from Member States to deny EU funding to organisations such as FEMYSO?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.9.2025) As elaborated in the Commission’s replies to written questions E-006476/20201 and Regulation3 for the award of funds. It carries out rigorous selection processes, including different checks on grant applicants based on objective criteria such as the exclusion criteria or the EU restrictive measures.

The Commission would like to refer the Honourable Members to previous replies related to funding of the Forum of European Muslim Youth and Student Organisations (FEMYSO) such as to written questions P-002185/2025 and E-001052/20254. The Commission is aware of the report of the French Ministry of Interior5. The Commission relies on information and reports provided by all Member States.

It is the responsibility of the Member States to take the necessary measures, including by addressing the national courts, in case of substantiated breaches of the law by an association registered under their jurisdiction taking into account the need to respect freedom of speech, freedom of association and freedom of religion and belief as well as the need to preserve an enabling framework for civil society and human rights defenders.
